en.name: Chapati (roti)
en.summary: Fresh chapatis keep 1–2 days at room temperature, 3–5 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, and 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F).
en.pantry: 1–2 days, and really they are a same-day food. Stack them hot in a cloth-lined casserole so their own steam keeps them pliable, and eat them the day they are made. A plain chapati has no fat and no preservative and is very thin, so it goes leathery within a day and moulds by the third in a warm kitchen — which is why it lasts nowhere near as long as a homemade loaf. Do not leave a stack out in a humid kitchen overnight.
en.fridge: 3–5 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with the cooled stack wrapped airtight. This is the honest trade: refrigeration stales bread faster than the counter does, because starch retrogradation runs quickest just above freezing, but it is what holds off mould — and since you are going to put a chapati back on a hot tawa anyway, the staling penalty is undone by the heat. Fifteen seconds a side on a dry pan, not the microwave, which steams them soggy and then leathery.
en.freezer: 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F) for best quality, a figure borrowed from commercial flatbreads. Interleave them with baking paper and freeze flat so they peel apart, then griddle from frozen. Kept continuously frozen they stay safe beyond that window — what the timeline describes is drying out and freezer burn, not safety. Squeeze the air out of the bag before it goes in.
en.thawing: No thawing needed: peel one off the stack and put it straight on a hot dry pan. If you must thaw, do it in the fridge and never on the counter.
spoilage: Fuzzy mould spots, which appear fast on a stack left out in humid weather.
A sour or fermented smell from a stack wrapped while still hot.
Hard, leathery edges that crack instead of folding.
Slimy or tacky surface between the chapatis in the stack.
tips: Cool them fully before wrapping, or the trapped steam will make them slimy.
Interleave with paper before freezing so you can take one at a time.
Reheat on a dry hot pan, never in the microwave.
Shop-bought packaged roti carries a printed date and behaves like commercial flatbread, not like this.

faq.a: 1–2 days at room temperature, 3–5 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 3–5 months frozen at −18 °C (0 °F).
Yes, 3–5 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Interleave them with paper, freeze flat, and griddle them straight from frozen.

faq.q: Is it bad to keep chapatis in the fridge?
faq.a: It stales them faster than the counter would, but it holds off mould and buys you days. Since you reheat them on a hot pan, the staling is reversed anyway.

zh.name: 印度薄餅
zh.summary: 現做的印度薄餅放室溫可放 1～2 天，4 °C 以下冷藏 3～5 天，−18 °C 冷凍 3～5 個月。
zh.pantry: 1～2 天，但老實說它是當天的食物。剛煎好就疊進鋪了布的有蓋鍋裡，靠自己的蒸氣維持柔軟，並在做的當天吃掉。原味薄餅沒有油脂也沒有防腐劑、又非常薄，所以一天內就會變得像皮革，在溫暖的廚房裡第三天就長霉——這也是為什麼它在室溫下撐不了自製麵包那麼久。潮濕的廚房裡，不要把一疊薄餅放在外面過夜。
zh.fridge: 放涼後密封包好，4 °C 以下 3～5 天。這裡的取捨很誠實：冷藏讓麵餅老化得比室溫更快，因為澱粉回凝在略高於冰點時跑得最快；但冷藏正是壓住霉的辦法——而既然你反正要把薄餅丟回熱鍋上，那份老化的代價會被熱直接抵消掉。乾鍋每面十五秒，不要微波；微波會先把它蒸軟，再讓它變成皮革。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 3～5 個月品質最好，這個數字是從市售薄餅借來的。每張之間夾一張烘焙紙、平放冷凍，之後才撕得開，要吃直接從冷凍上鍋煎。只要全程沒退冰，超過這個期限仍然安全——期限描述的是變乾和凍燒，不是安全。裝袋前把空氣壓出來。
zh.thawing: 不必解凍：從那疊裡撕一張下來，直接放上乾熱鍋。真的要解凍就放冷藏，絕對不要放室溫檯面。
spoilage: 長出絨毛狀霉點；潮濕天氣下擺在外面的一疊來得特別快。
還熱著就包起來的那疊，聞起來發酸或有發酵味。
邊緣又硬又韌，一折就裂。
疊在一起的餅之間變得黏滑或黏手。
tips: 完全放涼再包，否則困住的蒸氣會讓它們發黏。
冷凍前每張之間夾紙，才能一次只拿一張。
回熱用乾熱鍋，千萬不要微波。
超市買的包裝薄餅有印製日期，行為比較像市售薄餅，不是這一篇講的現做薄餅。

faq.a: 室溫 1～2 天，4 °C 以下冷藏 3～5 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 3～5 個月。
可以，−18 °C 下 3～5 個月。每張夾紙平放冷凍，要吃直接從冷凍上鍋煎。

faq.q: 印度薄餅放冷藏會不會不好？
faq.a: 會比放室溫老化得更快，但能壓住霉、多爭取好幾天。而且你反正要用熱鍋回熱，老化那部分會被抵消掉。
